title: Mario Meets Pareto
author: theanonymousone
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Finding the fastest driver is as simple as ranking them by their speed statistic. Here you might think that Bowser or Wario are a no-brainer. But you can't just rely on speed to find the optimal build. You have to consider one as well. Now, finding the best is not trivial anymore — you have to make trade-offs between

and Look closely though! You'll find out that some options are always dominated. Let's focus on this poor Koopa for instance. Cat Peach has more speed for the same acceleration, and Toadette has more acceleration for the same speed. Between you and me, if you want to win, never allow Koopa to sit in your kart! You can identify all efficient drivers that, unlike Koopa, are never dominated on both speed and acceleration. Together, they form what is called the Pareto front (or frontier). Mind you: not all elements of the frontier are equally good. You probably won't pick a driver sitting on the edge of the frontier because you want some balance between speed and acceleration. The Pareto efficiency is an objective criteria to filter out suboptimal choices, but you still need to make up your final decision. Given your play style and skills, you may put more weight on one statistic over the other. Those preferences will reveal the component on the frontier that suits you the best. Best : {}

comments.author: jerf
comments.textRawHtml:
This is a really important concept for developers.

One aspect for developers that I see quite often is the assertion that "We can't have X without giving up more Y", most commonly "we can't have more security without giving up on user experience". With the Pareto idea in mind, we can see that that statement is true, if and only if you are in fact on the Pareto frontier of security and user experience already.

However, many times these confident pronouncements are being made when the system under question is quite evidently not on the Pareto frontier in the first place and indeed you can get more of one without giving up the other.

Making it more tricky is that in business, you can never discard "money" as a dimension, so unless you're taking "money" as one of the dimensions in the original comparison you want to do, it sneaks its way in. Or, a composite time/money, or "cost to business", or some other similar concept, time & money aren't orthogonal and don't need to be treated as two separate dimensions in general, though you can if you want. Which puts you into the 3D case, and as the page says, that grows the frontier quite a lot, which is good in some ways and bad in others. Nevertheless, in my opinion it is still often the case that even in that space we are often making "tradeoffs" without checking that we're on the Pareto frontier in the first place.
comments.textZhHtml:
这对于开发人员来说是一个非常重要的概念。

对于开发人员来说，我经常看到的一个方面是这样的断言：“我们不能在不放弃更多 Y 的情况下拥有 X”，最常见的是“如果不放弃用户体验，我们就不能拥有更多的安全性”。考虑到帕累托思想，我们可以看到，这个说法是正确的，当且仅当您实际上已经处于安全和用户体验的帕累托前沿。

但是，很多时候，当所讨论的系统显然一开始就不在帕累托前沿，并且实际上您可以在不放弃另一个的情况下获得更多时，就会做出这些自信的声明。

更棘手的是，在商业中，您永远不能放弃“金钱”作为一个维度，因此除非您将“金钱”作为您想要进行的原始比较中的维度之一，否则它会悄悄进入。或者，时间/金钱的复合，或“业务成本”，或其他一些类似的概念，时间和金钱不是正交的，通常不需要被视为两个单独的维度，尽管如果您愿意，也可以这样做。这会让你进入 3D 情况，正如页面上所说，这使边界增长了很多，这在某些方面是好的，但在其他方面却是坏的。尽管如此，在我看来，即使在这个空间中，我们仍然经常进行“权衡”，而没有首先检查我们是否处于帕累托边界。

children.author: munchbunny
children.textRawHtml: Agreed with what you said, when you're only considering security and usability you're often not at a Pareto optimal state, but once you add cost into the picture you see a lot more cases of being on the Pareto optimal boundary, or at least in case where the next improvement only comes with significant effort (by re-platforming, for example).
children.textZhHtml: 同意你所说的，当你只考虑安全性和可用性时，你通常不会处于帕累托最优状态，但是一旦你将成本添加到图中，你会看到更多处于帕累托最优边界的情况，或者至少在下一次改进需要付出巨大努力才能实现的情况下（例如，通过重新构建平台）。

children.author: efavdb
children.textRawHtml: I guess that makes sense.  as you get to higher dimensions, most points sit very close to the surface.  So if we're trading off N things and N >> 1, expect to basically always be at the pareto boundary.
children.textZhHtml: 我想这是有道理的。  当你达到更高的维度时，大多数点都非常靠近表面。  因此，如果我们要权衡 N 个事物和 N >> 1，则期望基本上始终处于帕累托边界。

children.author: miki123211
children.textRawHtml:
On the other hand, we should recognize that, to put it plainly, not all dimensions on the frontier have the same level of importance.

Any technological and societal progress is going to have negative consequences. To give just one example, completely curing cancer will put many doctors (and other healthcare professionals who aren't paid as well as doctors are) out of a job. It will definitely cause at least a few children to go hungry. It will probably cause a few suicides when some oncologists start to "feel useless." This does not mean we shouldn't cure cancer if the opportunity arises.

Our society, driven by clickbait, rage and social media hot takes, tends to overweight the dimensions at which new technology makes things worse. There are many news stories about social-media-fueled teen suicides or AI datacenter water use, very few about how talking to family abroad no longer requires astronomical long-distance bills.
children.textZhHtml:
另一方面，我们应该认识到，简单地说，并不是所有前沿维度都具有相同的重要性。

任何技术和社会进步都会产生负面后果。仅举一个例子，彻底治愈癌症将使许多医生（以及其他薪资不如医生的医疗保健专业人员）失业。肯定会导致至少有几个孩子挨饿。当一些肿瘤学家开始“感觉自己一无是处”时，这可能会导致一些人自杀。这并不意味着如果有机会我们就不应该治愈癌症。

我们的社会在点击诱饵、愤怒和社交媒体热门话题的推动下，往往过度重视新技术使事情变得更糟的维度。有很多关于社交媒体引发的青少年自杀或人工智能数据中心用水的新闻报道，但很少有关于与国外家人交谈如何不再需要天文数字的长途电话费的新闻报道。

children.author: adrianN
children.textRawHtml: The article does talk about putting weights on the dimensions to account for different dimensions having different importance.
children.textZhHtml: 文章确实讨论了对维度赋予权重，以考虑具有不同重要性的不同维度。

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml: For one we need to start talking about taking off the weights from security dimension, because it's becoming ridiculously overemphasized for things where it frankly doesn't matter much for. All at the cost of "usability", which is a fancy word for saying people's time and effort, which is literally the only truly non-renewable, priceless resource we have.
children.textZhHtml: 首先，我们需要开始谈论从安全维度中减轻负担，因为对于坦率地说无关紧要的事情来说，它变得可笑地过分强调了。所有这些都是以“可用性”为代价的，这是一个花哨的词，用来形容人们的时间和精力，而这实际上是我们拥有的唯一真正不可再生、无价的资源。

children.author: adrianN
children.textRawHtml: My experience has been that security is mostly treated as some contractual obligation that has little benefit and just costs money so the minimum amount of effort that prevents charges of gross negligence is put in. But I’m glad to hear that apparently there are places that take it more seriously.

children.author: TeMPOraL
children.textRawHtml:
Passkeys, 2FA being deployed the more intensely the more trivial and non-critical for users a site is, mobile platforms getting absurdly locked down, naive takes on "lethal trifecta" sucking out whatever little air in AI discussions that was left by IP apologists". In the real world, everyone in this industry seems to be showing off pointing out potential vulnerabilities and security considerations in any new idea or concept that appears - as if that were something to be proud of, instead of a solemn duty that more than likely will just prevent a nice thing from existing in the first place.

From where I stand, the industry is obsessed with security, way past the point of rational thought.

密码、2FA 部署得越频繁，网站对用户来说就越琐碎和不重要，移动平台被荒谬地锁定，幼稚的“致命三重奏”吸走了人工智能讨论中 IP 辩护者留下的任何一点空气。”在现实世界中，这个行业的每个人似乎都在炫耀指出任何出现的新想法或概念中的潜在漏洞和安全考虑因素 - 好像这就是什么自豪，而不是一种庄严的义务，这种义务很可能从一开始就阻止美好事物的存在。

从我的立场来看，该行业痴迷于安全，远远超出了理性思考的范围。

children.author: jerf
children.textRawHtml: Yes, I don't mean to imply that this is some sort of clear majority situation or anything. I just mean that I've definitely both seen on HN and participated in real life in some conversations in which it was taken as given that we must give up one thing to get another when nobody had in fact established that we were on the Pareto frontier. Or, considered from a local point of view, whether the tradeoff really was inevitable. I have had cases where we could have had both, with no difficulty.
children.textZhHtml: 是的，我并不是想暗示这是某种明显的多数情况或其他情况。我只是说，我确实在 HN 上看到过，也参与过现实生活中的一些对话，在这些对话中，我们必须放弃一件事才能得到另一件事，而实际上没有人确定我们处于帕累托边界。或者，从局部的角度考虑，这种权衡是否真的是不可避免的。我遇到过这样的情况，我们可以毫无困难地两者兼而有之。

children.author: adrianN
children.textRawHtml: I’m very high dimensional spaces as they occur in real life projects with difficult to measure dimensions (eg how much does implementing something cost and how much does not implementing something cost) it seems very difficult to determine where you are in your space. Most companies run their product mostly on feels because anything else would quickly lead to analysis paralysis.
children.textZhHtml: 我是非常高维度的空间，因为它们出现在现实生活中的项目中，难以测量维度（例如，实施某项需要花费多少成本，不实施某项需要花费多少），似乎很难确定您在空间中的位置。大多数公司主要依靠感觉来运行他们的产品，因为其他任何东西都会很快导致分析瘫痪。

children.author: voidhorse
children.textRawHtml:
Yes, the difference between coding (writing software) and engineering (making informed trade offs about system design) is effectively bound up in analyses like those supported by concepts like pareto efficiency.

One should keep in mind though that not all problems have a neat solution. Many spaces have multiple efficient points that still need to be chosen from, and many pareto optimization problems actually become NP hard computationally when the problem is large enough.
children.textZhHtml:
是的，编码（编写软件）和工程（对系统设计进行明智的权衡）之间的区别实际上与帕累托效率等概念支持的分析紧密相关。

人们应该记住，并非所有问题都有一个简洁的解决方案。许多空间具有多个有效点，仍然需要从中进行选择，并且当问题足够大时，许多帕累托优化问题实际上在计算上变得NP困难。

children.author: ksclk
children.textRawHtml: Say someone wanted to transition from coding to engineering. What path would you have them take? What should they learn?
children.textZhHtml: 假设有人想从编码转向工程。你会让他们走哪条路？他们应该学习什么？

children.author: voidhorse
children.textRawHtml:
I would say start with software architecture books for large or highly distributed systems. This will get you thinking beyond code level to system component level with subject matter that's familiar.

From there I would round things out with general systems theory books and even dabble in some non-software engineering texts just to get a sense of how people reason about designing systems and evaluating trade-offs. That's just my two cents on it.
children.textZhHtml:
我想说从大型或高度分布式系统的软件架构书籍开始。这将使您的思考超越代码级别，进入系统组件级别，并使用熟悉的主题。

从那里我会用一般系统理论书籍来完善这些内容，甚至涉足一些非软件工程文本，只是为了了解人们如何推理设计系统和评估权衡。这只是我的两分钱。
